headline: A Shark's Homecoming: Why Bukangi Keeps Swimming Back
meta_description: After a dramatic eight-hour rescue operation, a dusky shark named Bukangi was guided out of a South Korean canal—only to swim back repeatedly.
summary_short: Bukangi, a three-metre dusky shark that captivated Busan, was freed from a canal but keeps returning to the waterway that became her unexpected home.
body:
When rescue workers spent more than eight hours carefully guiding a three-metre dusky shark named Bukangi out of a Busan canal on Wednesday, hundreds of fans cheered from the overlooking park. But within hours, the shark had broken through authorities' barrier and returned. Over the following days, Bukangi repeatedly circled back to the canal's mouth rather than venture permanently into open sea, leaving rescuers to fortify nets and continue monitoring her movements. The official rescue operation has now concluded, yet the enigma remains: why won't this celebrated shark leave?

Bukangi arrived in the south-eastern port city's canal a month earlier, drawing 1.6 million visitors and becoming an unofficial mascot. Residents and visitors held divided views about her fate. Some, like Cho Hannah, who travelled two hours from North Geongsang province to protest the rescue, believed the canal had become her home and feared she might be harmed in the open sea. Others worried that Bukangi's apparent injuries and gaunt appearance suggested she needed to leave—that remaining in the canal with falling water temperatures posed greater danger than freedom.

Experts believe Bukangi was initially drawn to the canal by unusually warm waters and abundant fish. As sea temperatures continue rising each year, Busan may welcome more sharks in the future. The real story here is not simply one of a trapped animal, but of a community divided by genuine care—each side hoping, in their own way, to protect a creature that had unexpectedly become part of their lives.
quick_facts: Three-metre dusky shark nicknamed Bukangi spotted in Busan canal
Eight-hour livestreamed rescue operation on Wednesday
1.6 million visitors attracted over one month
Shark repeatedly returned after being guided to open water
Attracted by warm waters and plentiful fish, say experts
